lesson.child_mission: Unit review connects First Fleet motives, colonial roles, effects on First Nations Peoples, resistance/survival, colonial expansion maps and daily-life evidence with multiple perspectives.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mini: one effect of settlement on First Nations Peoples; one respectful source habit.

FEEDBACK
e.g. loss of land/food access; use Community/published First Nations sources, no invention.

WATCH FOR
A colony-only celebration showcase without First Nations perspectives is incomplete.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Showcase pack: six cards covering motives, roles, FN effects, resistance/survival, map, daily life — each with source or verification tag. One-minute fair talk.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Showcase pack: six cards covering motives, roles, FN effects, resistance/survival, map, daily life — each with source or verification tag. One-minute fair talk. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using review on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: A colony-only celebration showcase without First Nations perspectives is incomplete.. Correction: e.g. loss of land/food access;. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: A colony-only celebration showcase without First Nations perspectives is incomplete. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating review on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with review, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about review with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for review. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

Unit review connects First Fleet motives, colonial roles, effects on First Nations Peoples, resistance/survival, colonial expansion maps and daily-life evidence with multiple perspectives.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
